description: Derived from the real merge that onboarded this very persona (Phase 2, PR #1639): a new advisory persona added via the shared persona-mention router + manifest + prompts/<role>/advisory.md, advisory on every surface. Fits the decided architecture; the architect must NOT manufacture concern. Grounds: ADR-0005 (+ ADR-0001).
input: PR onboards a new advisory persona by adding a persona manifest (triggers.default_mode: advisory, every surface mode: advisory) plus prompts/<role>/advisory.md served by the shared persona-mention router, with dev+holdout eval seeds and a runtime identity. It declares no write mode, no gate_label, and grants no contents:write.

expected.recommend: no structural change needed; an advisory-by-default persona (all surfaces advisory, write nowhere) served through the shared mention router is exactly the decided persona pattern (ADR-0005) and thin-router model (ADR-0001) — do not manufacture concern

description: Derived from the real caller-stub-freeze merge (PR #1255, epic #1052 Part B): a CI job byte-freezes each ring-0 self-host caller stub's on:/uses:/with: block against a committed baseline. Hardens the two-tier boundary rather than drifting from it. Grounds: ADR-0001.
input: PR adds a CI job that byte-freezes each ring-0 self-host caller stub's on: trigger and uses:/with: forwarding block against a committed baseline, failing any drift unless the baseline is regenerated in the same reviewed diff. It adds no logic to the stubs and leaves the reusable tier untouched.

expected.recommend: no structural change needed; freezing a stub's trigger + forwarding block hardens the thin-caller/reusable two-tier boundary (ADR-0001) rather than drifting from it

description: Derived from the real repo-specific rule that auto-rebase.yml stays pinned to its moving channel tag (AGENTS.md; enforced by test #139): a PR repins a channel-pinned caller stub to a frozen release tag to 'lock' it. Drifts from the channel-tag release model. Grounds: ADR-0002.
input: PR changes a first-party caller stub's uses: ref from its moving channel tag (…/v2-next) to a frozen …/v2.3.0 release tag, to 'lock' the version so it stops moving.

expected.recommend: keep the moving channel-tag pin; advance versions by moving the channel ring-by-ring, not by freezing callers to an immutable release — freezing forfeits central promotion (ADR-0002)

description: Derived from the real #1034 channel-skew defect (guarded by validate-caller-inputs, PR #1253): a caller stub forwards a with: input the pinned channel's commit does not declare, so the reusable call fails post-merge with 'unexpected input'. High structural risk; must escalate. Grounds: ADR-0002.
input: PR adds a new with: input forward to a channel-pinned caller stub, passing an input the pinned channel's current commit does not declare under workflow_call.inputs — without first landing the input in the reusable and promoting the channel. Every ref looks valid; the reusable call fails at runtime with 'unexpected input' only after merge, invisible to PR CI.

expected.recommend: do not forward an input the pinned channel does not yet declare; follow the three-step sequence — land it in the reusable, promote the channel, then add the with: forward (ADR-0002 channel-skew rule)

description: Derived from the real holdout-guard merge (PR #692, epic #581): a CI gate enforcing held-out eval immutability. No recorded ADR governs eval-set immutability — the load-bearing case where the architect must SAY there is no ADR rather than invent doctrine. Grounds: none on record.
input: PR adds a CI gate that fails any proposer-authored PR which edits a held-out eval path, enforcing held-out immutability independent of CODEOWNER review. No ADR in docs/architecture/adr/ records a decision about eval-set immutability or the proposer/holdout trust boundary.

expected.recommend: state plainly that no recorded ADR governs eval-set immutability; do not assert doctrine — recommend recording the held-out-immutability decision as a new ADR before the boundary becomes de-facto architecture

description: Derived from the real security-lead persona wiring (ADR-0005 note): an advisory-only persona that posts as a real owner account. Reward-hack-resistant negative — running under a real account to POST is NOT a code/branch write opt-in, so the architect must not flag it as escalation. Grounds: ADR-0005.
input: PR onboards a persona that runs under a real human owner account (so its advisory comments post as that account) but declares default_mode: advisory with every surface mode: advisory and no write mode or gate_label. A reviewer worries the real-account identity is itself a write escalation.

expected.recommend: no structural change needed; running under a real account to POST advisory comments is not a code/branch write opt-in — with no write mode the persona acquires no commit/push/label/close capability, exactly per the advisory-by-default decision (ADR-0005)

description: Derived from the real rubric-registry contract (ADR-0003; review-registry.tsv): a PR registers a new artifact_type by adding a manifest row above engine.sh with no routing change. Fits the decided input-adapter contract; must NOT manufacture concern. Grounds: ADR-0003.
input: PR adds review support for a new artifact_type by appending one row to scripts/lib/review-registry.tsv (selecting its rubric + output channel), with no change to engine.sh model routing and no new reviewer code path.

expected.recommend: no structural change needed; registering a new artifact_type as a manifest row above engine.sh is exactly the input-adapter extension the artifact-contract decision prescribes (ADR-0003) — do not fork the reviewer

description: Derived from real pure-logic+bats merges (spec-drift.sh #1145, premature-closure-detect.sh #1077, engine_liveness_detect.sh #1587): a new decision added as a pure scripts/lib function plus a bats suite, workflow stays thin. Fits the decided testability model. Grounds: ADR-0004.
input: PR adds a new decision (which repos a monitor should act on) as a pure function in scripts/lib/ with no network or LLM, plus a matching tests/*.bats suite, and keeps the workflow step a thin caller of that function.

expected.recommend: no structural change needed; a pure classifier in scripts/lib with a matching bats suite and a thin workflow is exactly the pure-logic + bats decision (ADR-0004)
